title: traffic pulse fader canary and degraded-mode automaton
author: Diego Alvarez
description: Motivation: We observe short-lived high-frequency traffic pulses from a subset of clients that produce transient tail-latency spikes which the existing canary detectors either ignore (too short) or treat as regressions (too sensitive). This PR introduces a "traffic pulse fader" probe and a small-state "degraded-mode automaton" that together: 1) detect high-frequency short-duration pulses using a sliding-event pulse detector tuned for burstiness, 2) apply a temporary smoothing window (fader) on aggregated latency percentiles to prevent premature canary-triggered rollbacks for pulses that self-resolve, and 3) transition the rollout guard into a degraded mode where stricter quorum and sanity checks are enforced before auto-rollbacks. The goal is to reduce noisy false positives while preserving fast response to sustained regressions. Design summary: - pulse detector: lightweight CWT-inspired heuristic that flags pulse candidates based on short-window throughput derivative and inter-arrival entropy (src/probers/pulse_fader.go) - fader: exponentially-weighted decay applied to percentile deltas that reduces short-lived spikes' impact on the canary score (evaluator/fader.py) - degraded-mode automaton: finite-state machine with states {NORMAL, SOFT_DEGRADED, HARD_DEGRADED} that escalates based on persistent signal across cohorts and enforces additional cross-slice consensus checks before rollback (config/canary_policy.yaml, src/automata/degraded_mode.py) Compatibility and safety: - New detector is opt-in via canary_policy flags; default config keeps existing behavior. - Observability: added dedicated metrics (canary.pulse.detected, canary.fader.decay_applied, canary.degraded_mode.state) and debug logs behind debug-level gating (docs/observability.md). Testing: - Unit tests for pulse detection edge cases and fader decay (tests/test_pulse_fader.py). - Integration harness run against replayed production traces including three known pulse incidents; added synthetic pulse generator in benchmark-lab/fixtures/pulse_traces.json. - CI run: initial lint/test failed due to race in snapshot test; fixed by adding controlled clock in tests. Rollout plan: - Deploy to staging Canary group A for 24h with metrics dashboard and alert thresholds adjusted; if no sustained regressions and reduced false positives seen, roll to global. - If degraded-mode engages in staging, ops will get a notification and human-in-the-loop will operate rollback controls; automatic rollbacks are disabled for SOFT_DEGRADED in first rollout. Checklist: - [x] Implementation for detector, fader, automaton - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Observability metrics and dashboards (draft) - [x] Config gating and feature flag - [x] Linear ticket ENG-4217 attached Related: mentions SUP-9021 where a customer reported frequent short spikes during traffic bursts, and links to prior canary work on burst handling. For reviewers: main behavioral change is the fader math and the automaton transitions; please focus on the escalation thresholds and the observability coverage.
commit_summary: Initial implementation of pulse detector and fader
Add degraded-mode automaton FSM and policy config
Fix: use monotonic clock in tests to avoid flakiness
review_comments: Sophie Barnes: Nice work — can you document the expected memory and CPU overhead of the pulse detector? Concerned about additional per-prober allocations.
Diego Alvarez: Added a microbenchmark in the PR description and included a note in docs. Detector uses fixed-size ring buffers; cost measured ~0.4% CPU at 10k rps in staging sim.
Marcus Kim: The decay constant choice is critical. Can we expose it as a per-canary override? Also please add more unit tests for corner-case decays.
Diego Alvarez: Made decay_k configurable in policy and added tests covering nil/edge values.
Leah Chen: CI flaked on snapshot diff; looks like timing-based nondeterminism. Suggest using a fake clock in tests (see comment).
Diego Alvarez: Switched tests to monotonic fake clock; pushed fix. CI green after rerun.
merge_notes: Squashed and merged after approvals from Sophie and Marcus. Kept commit message summarizing detector + automaton + observability. Feature gated in config; not enabled in default production rollout until staging validation completes.
release_notes: Introduce pulse-aware canary detector with temporary fader smoothing and a degraded-mode automaton to reduce false-positive rollbacks for short traffic bursts. Feature is opt-in via canary_policy and adds observability metrics.

Create dashboard tile for canary.pulse.detected and canary.fader.decay_applied
